measurement.subject: flood-zone
measurement.neverSampled: Both counties were resolved in full over the union roster of both stores.

denominatorCorrection.label: VERIFIED — the finding that removes the premise
denominatorCorrection.text: SS-W5's Travis rate of 0.04 percent was taken over 804,458 parcels. Only 27,584 Travis parcels carry a tier2 row at all, and only 4,145 of those name a zone; 23,438 carry status 'unavailable' with reason 'FEMA fetch skipped (--skip-fema)'. A disagreement is arithmetically impossible on the remainder, so the roster denominator measures tier2's COVERAGE and not its AGREEMENT.
denominatorCorrection.countingRule: comparable = entities where BOTH stores NAME a value. One entity contributes at most one count.
denominatorCorrection.consequence: 0.70 percentage points apart, not 200x. The claim that the disagreement tracks the snapshot rather than the geography rested entirely on a contrast that the denominators remove. Both numerators were re-derived independently by this lane and match SS-W5's 5,424 and 332 exactly — SS-W5's counting was right; only its denominator travelled without its rule.

verdictOnThePrediction.predicted: Bastrop's 8.69 percent is mostly staleness and collapses on refresh; Travis's 0.04 percent is mostly split parcels.
verdictOnThePrediction.measured: FALSIFIED IN BOTH HALVES. Staleness accounts for 0 of 5,424 Bastrop disagreements, so a refresh moves nothing. Split parcels account for 0 of 332 Travis disagreements; all 42 split parcels found anywhere are in Bastrop.
verdictOnThePrediction.preRegisteredBand: CP1 pre-registered, before the run, that the two counties would land within a few points of each other and that the tile-sampling artifact would dominate in both. The result is inside that band: 8.71 against 8.01, with the artifact at 99.08 percent.
verdictOnThePrediction.note: Reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome per DEV_PROCESS 3.2. The measurement was not tuned toward the pre-registered expectation; the classifier's own firing tests were written before any county was run.

causeOfEveryDisagreement.countingRule: every disagreement in both counties, adjudicated against NFHL_48_20260101 by re-running BOTH stores' sample points and the parcel polygon in PostGIS. Nothing was sampled and nothing was extrapolated.
causeOfEveryDisagreement.mechanism: The tier2 bake quantises each parcel centroid to a 0.005-degree tile, issues ONE live FEMA ArcGIS point query at the tile CENTRE, and reuses that answer for every parcel in the tile. Measured separation between the two stores' sample points over adjudicated disagreements: Bastrop min 12.4 m, median 226.5 m, max 366.4 m; Travis min 31.1 m, median 202.2 m, max 357.7 m. The Bastrop maximum lands on the half-diagonal of a 0.005-degree tile at 30N, which is what the mechanism predicts and is the strongest confirmation available that the reconstruction is right.

whoIsRightAboutTheParcel.label: VERIFIED — the number the retirement decision turns on
whoIsRightAboutTheParcel.text: Ground truth at the parcel centroid matches the ATOM in 5,703 of 5,703 sampling-point cases and 11 of 11 vintage-undecidable cases. It matches TIER2 in ZERO cases of either class. The 42 split parcels are genuinely both (truth at the centroid falls on store A's side in 10, store B's in 30, and on a third zone in 2 — which is what a split parcel looks like, not a tie-break).
whoIsRightAboutTheParcel.countingRule: 'truth' is the NFHL zone at store A's sample point under NFHL_48_20260101, over adjudicated disagreements only.
whoIsRightAboutTheParcel.consequence: There is no case in either county where tier2 is right about the parcel and the atom is wrong. That is not a close call between two stores; it is one store answering the question and one store answering a nearby question.

customerFacingCost.label: VERIFIED
customerFacingCost.text: 1,995 parcels across the two counties where tier2 names a zone OUTSIDE the special flood hazard area and the atom names one inside it. Bastrop 1,940, Travis 55.
customerFacingCost.countingRule: over disagreements only; SFHA membership decided by the leading letter of the FEMA zone code (A and V families inside, X and D outside).
customerFacingCost.otherDirection: 3,670 parcels where tier2 overstates the hazard (Bastrop 3,393, Travis 277), plus 91 where both are inside the SFHA but name different zones.
customerFacingCost.why_it_matters: Understating is the dangerous direction: it tells a reader there is no flood risk on a parcel whose centroid is in the floodplain. This is not currently reaching a browser (SS-W5, P-43), which is the only reason it is a finding rather than an incident — and it means the serving bug SS-W5 found was, accidentally, the thing preventing it.

instrumentSelfCheck.label: VERIFIED
instrumentSelfCheck.declaredDeviation: The flood-hazard-fact atom does not record the point it evaluated, so this instrument uses the centroid the tier2 bake recorded as a stand-in for store A's sample point. The two are computed by different ringCentroid implementations in different repos.
instrumentSelfCheck.check: Ground truth at the stand-in point reproduces the atom's OWN recorded zone in 5,392 of 5,424 Bastrop adjudications (99.41 percent) and 332 of 332 Travis adjudications (100 percent).
instrumentSelfCheck.reading: A low rate here would have invalidated every explained-by-sampling-point verdict in this report. It is high, and the residual 0.59 percent is almost exactly the split-subject plus vintage-undecidable population, which is where a centroid legitimately falls in a different zone than the stored value. The deviation is sound on evidence, not on hope.

tier2VintageFieldAudit.label: VERIFIED
tier2VintageFieldAudit.text: 89,841 tier2 rows across the two counties carry a provenance.vintage, and 89,841 of them are ISO instants equal to the bake's own clock. Not one is an NFHL edition string.
tier2VintageFieldAudit.consequence: The dispatch's vintage-versus-split fork is undecidable on the tier2 side by construction. A lane that applied it mechanically would have read two unlike strings as two different editions and reported 5,424 Bastrop staleness cases that do not exist.

adversarialReviewOfThisLaneSOwnWork: The strongest objection to the sampling-point verdict is that the instrument reconstructs the tier2 bake's tiling rule from another repo's source rather than reading a recorded sample point. That objection is answered by evidence and not by argument: the reconstruction predicts a maximum separation of one tile half-diagonal, and the measured Bastrop maximum is 366.4 m against a predicted ~366 m. A wrong reconstruction would not land on its own bound.

The second objection is that 'explained-by-sampling-point' could absorb a genuine conflict by construction. It cannot: the class requires ground truth at BOTH points to reproduce BOTH stores independently, which is a two-sided test. A case where truth matched only one side falls through to edition-differs or vintage-undecidable, and a case matching neither falls through to genuine-conflict. Both of those paths have firing tests and both returned non-zero or zero for stated reasons.

The third objection is that the classifier could be folding FEMA zone families to shrink the disagreement count. It does not, and there is a test asserting AE is not folded into A and X is not folded into X500.

Where this lane is WEAKEST: the measurement covers 2 of the 10 counties that carry tier2 rows, chosen because they are the two the dispatch names. The remaining 8 (48209, 48309, 48091, 48187, 48029, 48027, 48055, 48491) hold 516,573 tier2 rows and are unmeasured. Nothing here should be read as a statewide flood-divergence rate; it is a two-county rate whose mechanism is statewide because the mechanism is in the bake, not in the geography.

Also weak: 7 of the 8 registered duplicate subjects have no measurement pass. The detector NAMES them and the runner refuses them with an explicit error rather than returning zero, which is the honest failure mode, but 'inventoried' is not 'measured' and the close must not blur the two.

The 11 vintage-undecidable Bastrop cases: the atom matches ground truth at every point tested and the parcel lies wholly in one zone, so tier2 is simply wrong there. Five of the eleven are consecutive prop ids (8727948, 8727992, 8727993, 8727994, 8727996), which suggests one bad tile rather than eleven independent errors — untested.
